connection: Session 21 can filter, order, project, and total clock entries. No WorkSummary type exists yet, so this session explicitly creates the report result before using GroupBy and Join.
objectives: Create the WorkSummary result type before querying into it.
Use GroupBy to partition completed entries by employee.
Aggregate each group into total hours.
Use Join to correlate independent employee and summary sequences by ID.

visuals.title: GroupBy creates one bucket per employee
visuals.explanation: Every completed ClockEntry is routed to the group whose key equals its EmployeeId.

visuals.title: Each group becomes one WorkSummary
visuals.explanation: Select converts a group key and its summed durations into a report result.

visuals.title: Join matches two independent sequences
visuals.explanation: Employee IDs connect employee names to WorkSummary totals without embedding an Employee object in the report.

visuals.title: The report is materialized deliberately
visuals.explanation: ToList creates the finished report snapshot after filtering, grouping, projection, and ordering.

preQuiz.prompt: What becomes the key of each clock-entry group?
Why must WorkSummary be created in this session?
preQuiz.explanation: The lesson must not assume a missing result type.

preQuiz.prompt: What does an inner Join produce for an employee with no summary?
preQuiz.explanation: An inner join returns only matching keys.

concept.title: GroupBy creates employee buckets
paragraphs: After removing open entries, GroupBy(entry => entry.EmployeeId) creates one bucket for each EmployeeId. group.Key is the employee ID written on that bucket; enumerating group produces that employee's ClockEntry objects.
GroupBy does not create nested database rows or clone ClockEntry objects. It organizes the current sequence into groups so each employee's entries can be aggregated together.
Before grouping: Employee 1 — 8 hours; Employee 2 — 5 hours; Employee 1 — 7 hours. After grouping: Employee 1 bucket — 8 and 7; Employee 2 bucket — 5.

concept.title: Select turns each bucket into one WorkSummary
paragraphs: Select receives one entire employee bucket at a time. group.Key supplies WorkSummary.EmployeeId, while Sum collapses every duration inside that bucket into one total.

After projection, the example becomes Employee 1 — 15 total hours and Employee 2 — 5 total hours. The learner's GetDuration returns TimeSpan?, so ?. safely reads TotalHours and ?? supplies the non-null double WorkSummary requires.
OrderBy returns another sequence. ToList then executes the pipeline and stores a finished report snapshot. A List still supports later LINQ because it implements IEnumerable.

concept.title: Join combines values from matching objects
paragraphs: Employee supplies the name. WorkSummary supplies the hours. The matching employee ID connects them. If the output needed only employee names, Select would be enough; Join exists because the final label needs values from both objects.

Read Join's four arguments in this order: Second collection. First key. Second key. Final result. Here those become summaries, employee.Identity, summary.EmployeeId, and the label built from employee.Name plus summary.Hours.

Join is an inner join. If Employee.Identity is 1 while WorkSummary.EmployeeId is 19, there is no matching pair and therefore no label. The App demonstration deliberately uses employeeId for both sides.
Optional editor practice: Side Lab 01B includes a focused exercise for reading Join's generic IntelliSense signature one parameter at a time instead of memorizing it.
concept.code:
IEnumerable<string> labels = employees.Join(
    summaries,                         // second collection
    employee => employee.Identity,     // first key
    summary => summary.EmployeeId,     // second key
    (employee, summary) =>              // final result
        $"{employee.Name}: {summary.Hours:F1} hours");

lab.objective: Create a WorkSummary result type, group completed entries into per-employee totals, then join those totals to employee names.
lab.startingCondition: Employee, ClockEntry, PayrollService, and the Session 21 LINQ queries exist. The learner's source uses Models and Services folders, no explicit namespaces, Clockout spelling, Employee.Identity/Name, and TimeSpan? GetDuration(). Session 22 intentionally creates the Reports folder, WorkSummary, and ClockEntryAnalytics.
steps: Create src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain/Reports because the learner's current Domain project does not contain that folder yet.
Create src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain/Reports/WorkSummary.cs; do not add a namespace because the learner's existing Domain source does not use explicit namespaces.
In WorkSummary.cs, declare a public sealed class named WorkSummary. Remember: public allows App to use the class, and sealed prevents another class from inheriting from it.
In WorkSummary, add a public get-only int property named EmployeeId.
In WorkSummary, add a public get-only double property named Hours. Remember: double is appropriate for measured fractional hours; use decimal for money.
Add a public WorkSummary constructor with int employeeId and double hours parameters.
In the WorkSummary constructor, assign employeeId to EmployeeId.
In the WorkSummary constructor, assign hours to Hours.
Build the Domain project before starting the query class.
Create src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain/Reports/ClockEntryAnalytics.cs; do not add a namespace.
In ClockEntryAnalytics.cs, declare a public static class named ClockEntryAnalytics.
Add a public static HoursByEmployee method that accepts IEnumerable<ClockEntry> entries, returns IReadOnlyList<WorkSummary>, and temporarily throws NotImplementedException.

In HoursByEmployee, call Where on entries, keep entries whose Clockout property is not null, and store the new sequence in IEnumerable<ClockEntry> completedEntries. Remember from Session 21: new sequence, same ClockEntry objects.
Call GroupBy on completedEntries using entry.EmployeeId as the key, then store the returned buckets in a variable named employeeGroups.
Call Select on employeeGroups and create one WorkSummary per group using group.Key and group.Sum(entry => entry.GetDuration()?.TotalHours ?? 0); store the returned sequence in summaries.
Call OrderBy on summaries using summary.EmployeeId and store the returned sequence in orderedSummaries.
Call ToList on orderedSummaries and return the resulting report snapshot instead of throwing NotImplementedException.

Add a public static EmployeeLabels method that accepts IEnumerable<Employee> employees and IEnumerable<WorkSummary> summaries, returns IEnumerable<string>, and temporarily throws NotImplementedException.
In EmployeeLabels, begin employees.Join and pass summaries as the second sequence. Memory anchor: second collection, first key, second key, final result.
Add employee => employee.Identity as Join's first-sequence key selector.
Add summary => summary.EmployeeId as Join's second-sequence key selector.
Add (employee, summary) => $"{employee.Name}: {summary.Hours:F1} hours" as Join's final-result selector; store the returned sequence in IEnumerable<string> labels.
Return labels instead of throwing NotImplementedException.
Open src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.App/Program.cs and preserve all earlier session code.

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: The solution uses the learner source's no-namespace style, Clockout spelling, nullable GetDuration return type, and Employee.Identity/Name members. The App setup deliberately uses one matching employee ID.

Every referenced application artifact was created in this session or an earlier session.
Earlier production code, tests, and ScratchPad experiments remain intact.

postQuiz.prompt: Why filter open entries before GroupBy and Sum?
postQuiz.explanation: The aggregation must only call GetDuration on completed entries.

postQuiz.prompt: What does Select receive after GroupBy?
postQuiz.explanation: Each grouping has a Key and the entries for that key.
The shared identity establishes the relationship.

reflections: Why is WorkSummary a report result instead of another repository?
What does GroupBy remove from a manual nested-loop solution?
Would an employee with no entries need an inner join or a left join?
whatBreaks: Without WorkSummary the projection has no declared result type. Grouping before removing open entries lets GetDuration encounter incomplete data. Discarding any LINQ result loses that stage's new sequence. If Employee.Identity does not match WorkSummary.EmployeeId, the inner Join correctly returns no label.
summary: Session 22 now creates WorkSummary before using it, then builds a completed-entry report with GroupBy, Sum, ordering, and Join. Nothing is described as pre-existing unless an earlier session actually created it.
